purpose: Bepotastine besilate eye drops are used to relieve itchy eyes caused by eye allergies. They help with symptoms like redness, watering, and that annoying itchy feeling you get from things like pollen, pet dander, or dust. It is safe for adults and children 2 years and older.
how_it_works: Your body releases a chemical called histamine when it comes into contact with something you are allergic to, and that histamine is what causes your eyes to itch. Bepotastine works by blocking the histamine receptors in your eyes so the histamine cannot trigger that itchy reaction. Think of it like putting a lock on the door so histamine cannot get in and cause trouble.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a mild, temporary bitter taste in your mouth right after using the drops. You might also notice a brief mild stinging or burning sensation in your eye when you first put the drops in. Some people experience mild eye redness or headache as well.
warnings: Do not wear soft contact lenses when you put the drops in — wait at least 10 minutes before putting your contacts back in. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have any other eye conditions. Avoid touching the tip of the bottle to your eye or any surface to keep it clean and germ-free. If your eye symptoms do not improve or get worse, check back with your doctor.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in each affected eye twice a day. Try to use it at the same times each day, such as morning and evening. Shake the bottle gently before each use and wash your hands before putting in the drops.
